doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: John Williams on piano with Max Roach and Cannonball; a teacher at Florida State
summary: Jones tells of discovering that Star Wars composer John Williams played bebop piano on a 1955 record with Max Roach and Cannonball, then he and Baker try to recall Cannonball's Florida teacher.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: . . . and I’m trying to get the liner notes straight. So we go back, and I look at the personnel on it. I think Max Roach and Paul Chambers, Cannonball, and on piano I see John Williams. Wait a minute. Aw, it couldn’t be. It was. Star Wars Johnny Williams on piano, playing bebop. Look at the credits inside. I’m serious. Look at the credits inside. I couldn’t believe it. I didn’t believe it when I first saw it. Then I found a picture. There’s John, with hair, in 1955 . . .
You know Cannon graduated from Florida State when he was at 17 years old.
The guy that has the band.
A classic teacher down there. He used to talk about him all the time.
He’s legendary. All of a sudden I can’t think.
Oh yes, please. This is important.
